chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya said:
I was in Faid and walked with Ali ibn Bilal to the grave of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee'. He said, and Ali ibn Bilal said to me: The master of this grave said from al-Rida (peace be upon him):

"Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother from any direction, places his hand [on the grave], and recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-qadr' seven times, he will be safe from the greatest terror."

key_terms.إِنّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْر: The opening verse of Surah Al-Qadr, meaning 'Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Decree.'
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida, referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The greatest terror, referring to the awe of the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْقَبْرِ: The master of this grave, referring to the deceased buried there.
key_terms.فَيْدَ: A place name, likely Faid in Khorasan or nearby.
key_terms.قَبْرَ أَخِيهِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: The grave of his believing brother.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice and reward for visiting a believer's grave according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the intercessory role of the Imams, specifically linking the practice to Imam al-Rida (AS), thereby elevating the visitation of believers' graves to a means of spiritual security. The specific recitation of the 'Night of Decree' verse seven times connects the individual's journey to the cosmic significance of divine decree and salvation, offering protection from the 'greatest terror' (al-faza' al-akbar) during the final resurrection.
